answer: Latency-signed admission windows. Each new identity must submit its first transactions inside a randomly assigned narrow window, timed against a periodic network beacon. Clients learn their slot from a shared vault of commitments, so honest agents wait as instructed. Because windows are narrow and unannounced, an attacker cannot precompute or batch-launch many identities; each probe requires a fresh violet-tagged timing proof. The cost is repeated low-latency probing plus forfeited admissions per missed window.
